user.title: Solar Smart Miner — Solar & Grid Setup
user.description: Pick the sensor that reports solar production — or your net grid meter. The house consumption sensor (miners included) is optional: skip it if you only have a net grid meter. The OpenRouter key and model are optional too; without a key the controller still runs rule-based.

data.solar_production_entity: Solar production or net grid power sensor
data.openrouter_model: OpenRouter model (free models listed; any model id works)

optional_sensors.title: Solar Smart Miner — Optional Sensors
optional_sensors.description: Optionally select a battery state-of-charge sensor. Leave blank if you have no battery.

safety_thresholds.title: Solar Smart Miner — Safety Thresholds
safety_thresholds.description: Set the target temperature and its tolerance, and the battery floor. Below the target a miner may step up; up to target + tolerance it holds; at or above it steps down one step. Below the battery floor every miner stops.

init.title: Solar Smart Miner — Options
init.description: Miners are picked up automatically from hass-miner. Saving any section reloads the integration — no restart required.

edit_settings.title: Solar Smart Miner — Edit Settings
edit_settings.description: Adjust runtime settings. Saving reloads the integration — no restart required.

data.control_mode: Control mode (Manual: apply the proposal with the button; Automatic: applied every cycle)
data.mock_solar_enabled: Use Forecast.Solar as mock solar data (development only)
data.mock_consumption_enabled: Use total miner power as mock grid consumption (development only)

data_description.temp_target: Below this a miner may step up if there is energy. From here up to target + tolerance it holds, even with spare energy.
data_description.temp_tolerance: At or above target + tolerance a miner steps down one step. The miner's own temperature cutoff stays the last line of defense.
data_description.import_min: Without a battery, a small steady grid import is the only proof that all the solar is used: at 0 W a throttled inverter hides what the panels could give. Below this import Solar-follow adds one increment (starts a stopped miner at its lowest step first, else raises one miner one step). Default 200 W.
data_description.import_max: Between the minimum and this, Solar-follow holds; above it, it steps down (after the step-down delay). Keep the range at least one power step (200 W) wide. Default 400 W.
data_description.step_down_delay_minutes: How long the import must stay above the maximum before Solar-follow steps down, so a passing cloud costs no restart. Default 5.
data_description.morning_step_down_delay_minutes: The same during sunrise, while production is still rising (not a time of day): a miner started early may import for a while, the sun catches up. Default 30.
data_description.low_voltage_v: Only with a voltage sensor (Configure → Sensors). Low voltage means too much load on the supply: below this for the time below, one miner stops (the hungriest), then the next only after it has stopped and the voltage is still low. Default 210 V (a 230 V supply).
data_description.voltage_debounce_s: So a single dip changes nothing. Counted again after every change. Default 60 s.
data_description.ramp_lock_minutes: After any change every miner holds at most this long while the changed one restarts; it ends earlier once that one mines again at its new limit. Depends on the miner type. Default 4 minutes.
data_description.power_steps: Every power-limit change restarts the miner, and a wattage it has never run takes up to an hour to tune, so limits only ever move between these steps. Each miner uses the steps inside its own range. Default: 900 to 2500 in 200 W steps.

edit_sensors.title: Solar Smart Miner — Sensors
edit_sensors.description: Change the entities chosen during setup. Leave the house consumption sensor empty if you only have a net grid meter. The battery and forecast sensors are shown to the AI and written to its log. The actual PV output is also used to estimate the import when the grid meter is lost, and the voltage sensor (optional) by the low-voltage rule. Saving reloads the integration.

data.solar_production_entity: Solar production or net grid power sensor
data.forecast_power_next_hour_entity: Forecast: PV power next hour, W (optional)
data.forecast_energy_remaining_entity: Forecast: PV energy left today, kWh (optional)

edit_farm.title: Solar Smart Miner — Farm
edit_farm.description: What this installation is. The AI is told these in every request (they are context, never rules), and the base load is used when the grid meter is lost. Leave a field empty if it doesn't apply. Measurements and notes go to the file solar_smart_miner/farm.yaml in your Home Assistant config folder (created on first setup, with an example); it survives updates. Saving reloads the integration.

data.farm_schedule_automations: Schedule automations that also switch the miners

data_description.farm_inverters: For example: 3 × 5 kW, 15 kW in total.
data_description.farm_export: zero_export: the inverters hold their output to the load (the meter can't show spare sun). export_allowed: surplus goes to the grid.
data_description.farm_battery: none or present. The battery profiles are not built yet.
data_description.farm_temperature_cutoff: The firmware's own limit; the integration doesn't manage it.
data_description.farm_base_load: About how much the house draws besides the miners, in W.
data_description.farm_schedule_automations: Automations that pause or resume the miners at fixed hours. Switch them off before Automatic mode: two controllers fight.

edit_ai.title: Solar Smart Miner — AI (OpenRouter)
edit_ai.description: The AI reviews each decision and comments on it; it never changes the miners. Free models are rate-limited, so it is only asked every few minutes. Saving reloads the integration.

data_description.openrouter_api_key: Stored hidden. Clear it to turn the AI off.
data_description.openrouter_model: Free models are listed; you can also type any OpenRouter model id. 'openrouter/free' picks an available free model for you.
data_description.ai_interval: Default 60 s, minimum 10 s. Free models allow only a limited number of requests per day, so a short interval may need a paid model.
